## Clinical background

[Cryptococcosis in kidney transplant recipients](https://academic.oup.com/ofid/article/12/5/ofaf263/8121609) is uncommon but potentially catastrophic. When [transmission occurs through the donor](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8096655/), it often presents early after transplant, may involve the central nervous system, and is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality despite treatment.

The costs of cryptococcus after solid organ transplant are unclear.  Although studies have quantified the cost of a single hospitalization for cryptococcus,
no study to date has estimated the total excess cost of care due to cryptococcus.

## What this analysis does

This project uses the [**United States Renal Data System**](https://www.niddk.nih.gov/about-niddk/strategic-plans-reports/usrds) to analyze the impact of cryptococcus on costs.



## Study timeline and cost trajectories {#study-timeline}

@fig-cost-timeline illustrates how the planned study windows relate to case and control costs. The 365-day eligibility lookback is longer than the monthly cost-outcome window. Disease-related care and diagnostic workup can raise costs before the recorded diagnosis, so the prediagnosis trajectory is part of what the study aims to describe.

Earlier dashed curves provide context outside that panel. Shaded differences are illustrative and do not establish causal attribution.](quarto/assets/integrated-cost-timeline.svg){#fig-cost-timeline width=100% fig-alt="Line diagram of mean costs over time for cases and controls. [Open the figure at full size](quarto/assets/integrated-cost-timeline.svg).

For cases, time zero is the first qualifying diagnosis claim; controls are aligned at the same time since their most recent transplant, so their calendar dates may differ. The figure explains the intended windows, not the completeness of observation: coverage loss, death, and partial months require the handling specified in the [analysis plan](quarto/analysis-plan.qmd). Earlier costs may also inform planned matching covariates; they are outside the monthly outcome panel shown here.

## Methods

Each patient diagnosed with cryptococcosis (a *case*) is compared with up to two similar recipients who have reached the same time since transplant without being diagnosed (*controls*). Cases and controls are followed for 12 months from the same starting point, and the difference in their Medicare payments is the excess cost of cryptococcosis.

The [Study design and methods](quarto/study_overview.qmd) pages set out who is studied, how cases are found, how controls are matched, how costs are built and how they are analysed, with what the plan specifies and where the code stands.

## Reproducibility

The complete source code used to perform the full analysis and generate the tables and figures is publicly available at this [GitHub repo](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Cryptococcus-cost-analysis).  The R script `R/main.R` will run the R subscripts needed for this analysis in the order they are to be run.  Model assumptions, parameter values, and analytic workflows are documented in the repository to facilitate transparency and reuse. The USRDS data are restricted, so the analysis can be rerun only by an analyst with authorized access to them.
